2027-01-01.title: The Naming of our Lord · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.alt: Feast of the Naming of our Lord, eight days after Yaldo. New Year begins. Also the World Day of Peace in the universal Church.
2027-01-01.verse: After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised according to the Law and given his name: Jesus, “the name given by the angel before he was conceived”. The Son of God enters fully into the covenant of his people and receives a name that is a mission: Yeshua, “the Lord saves”. As the angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).

At the start of a new year the Church gives us not a resolution but a Name. St Peter would later proclaim: “There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). Every year, every plan, every fear can be placed under this Name.

St Paul's reading tells us how to begin anew: “put away your former way of life, your old self… and clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness” (Ephesians 4:22–24). A new calendar does not make a new person; Christ does. The New Year is a chance to put on Christ again.

Luke also says that Mary and Joseph brought the Child to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, offering the sacrifice of the poor, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”. The Holy Family begins every new stage by offering it to God. So may we offer this year to him.
conn: Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12) marked entry into Abraham's covenant. For Christians the eighth day became the day of the Resurrection and of the new creation.
Jesus is the same name as Joshua, who led Israel into the promised land (Joshua 1:1–9). Jesus leads us into the true promised land.
Paul sings that God gave Christ “the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend” (Philippians 2:9–10).
The two birds (Leviticus 12:8) show that the Holy Family was poor. The Son of God was born among the poor.
altar: We begin the new year at the altar, where the Name of Jesus is invoked over bread and wine and he becomes present. To receive Holy Communion on the first day of the year is to place the whole year in his hands.
outline: New Year greetings: what do people usually wish for? Health, wealth, success.
Point 1 · A Name, not a wish
Jesus: “the Lord saves”. Begin the year under his Name.
Point 2 · Put on the new self
Ephesians 4: a new year needs a new heart, not only a new calendar.
Like Mary and Joseph presenting the Child, offer the year to God.
World Day of Peace: pray and work for peace in families and nations.
“Jesus, I begin this year in your Name.”
live: Begin each day with the Name
Begin each morning this year with the sign of the cross and the prayer “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me.”
One old habit to put off (Ephesians 4:22)
Name one habit of the “old self” to leave behind this year, and one virtue to put on.
Ask the priest to bless your home during the season of Denho, or bless it yourselves with prayer and holy water.
fathers: The name of Jesus is light, food and medicine: “Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, a song of joy in the heart” (Sermons on the Song of Songs 15).
He praises the Name of the Son, sweet to those who love him, and the circumcision of the Lord who fulfilled the Law in himself (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Jesus means “God saves”; the name of Jesus contains everything; it is at the heart of Christian prayer.
The circumcision of Jesus is the sign of his incorporation into Abraham's descendants and prefigures Christian Baptism.
Message for the World Day of Peace
Each year on 1 January the Pope issues a message for peace; read it on vatican.va (see Papal documents).
saints: 2 Jan: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregory; name day of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis. 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, at your Naming you received the Name that saves. We begin this year in your Name: forgive our past, clothe us with the new self, bless our families and our work, and give peace to our world. Amen.

quick: Begin the year with a Name, not just a wish.
Put off the old self and put on the new.
2027-01-01.action: Name one old habit to leave behind and one virtue to put on this year.
2027-01-01.question: Under whose name will I live this year?
2027-01-01.special: The Naming of our Lord and New Year's Day. World Day of Peace.
illus: In many Kerala homes the first thing written in a new notebook or account book is a cross, or “Jesus” at the top of the first page. It is a small act of faith: everything that follows is placed under his Name.

family.explain: When Jesus was eight days old, Mary and Joseph gave him the name the angel had told them: Jesus, which means “God saves”.
family.intention: We offer this new year to Jesus and pray for peace in our family and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing will each of us try to do this year?”

catechism: Prayer in the name of Jesus.
kidsaint: A bishop in Caesarea who built a whole “new city” for the poor and sick, with hospitals and kitchens. Lesson: begin the new year by helping someone in need.
term: Jesus (Yeshua) means “the Lord saves”. Christians pray in this Name, bow at it, and begin their work under it. The ancient Jesus Prayer is: “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
termMore: Jewish boys were circumcised and named on the eighth day (Leviticus 12:3). The feast falls on 1 January, the octave day of Yaldo, which is also the civil New Year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on the eighth day you received the name that means God saves. We begin this new year in your name. Amen.
share: He was called Jesus (Luke 2:21). What does the name of Jesus mean to me?
Clothe yourselves with the new self (Ephesians 4:24). What old habit do I want to leave behind this year?
Mary and Joseph did everything the law required (Luke 2:22–24). How can our family begin the year in obedience to God?
pm.resp: Jesus, Son of God, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church at the beginning of the new year.
For peace in the world on this first day of the year.
For our families, that we may live this year in the name of Jesus.
For those who begin the year in sickness, grief or want.
For our group, that we may grow in prayer this year.
pm.close: Father, your Son received the name above every name. Bless this new year and keep us in his name. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed New Year to all of you! On this first day of the year, the Church celebrates the Naming of our Lord. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and given the name the angel had announced: Jesus.

In Hebrew, Jesus means “the Lord saves”. The angel told Joseph: “you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.” So on New Year's Day the Church does not give us a list of resolutions; she gives us a Name. St Peter says: “There is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.”

St Paul tells us what a real new beginning looks like: put away the old self, and clothe yourselves with the new self, created in the likeness of God. A new calendar does not make a new person. Only Christ makes us new. Let each of us name one old habit to put off, and one virtue to put on, this year.

And like Mary and Joseph, who brought the Child to offer him to the Lord, let us offer this whole year to God: our families, our work, our health, our plans. Today is also the World Day of Peace. May the Prince of Peace give peace to our homes and to our world. Jesus, we begin this year in your Name. Amen.
kids: Children, happy New Year! Today we remember the day baby Jesus got his name. Do you know what “Jesus” means? “God saves!”
Mary and Joseph gave him that name because an angel told them to. Jesus came to save us and help us be good.
This year, let's start every day by saying: “Jesus, I love you!” Let's say it together now: “Jesus, I love you!”

intro: On the eighth day the Child received the name Jesus, which means “the Lord saves”. We begin the year by calling on that name.

sub: The angel chose it before his birth (Matthew 1:21).
Mary and Joseph obeyed.
His name tells us his mission.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your own baptismal name.

sub: He humbled himself to the cross.
God exalted him.
Every knee shall bend.
points.apply: Bow your head whenever the name of Jesus is spoken at the Holy Qurbono.

sub: Peter heals in Jesus' name.
Salvation in no one else.
A year lived in his name.
points.apply: Begin each day this year with the name of Jesus.

concl: The name of Jesus is our programme for the new year: God saves.
Whatever this year holds, we face it in his name.
opts.resolve: This year I will begin and end each day by calling on the name of Jesus.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to all of you. On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21). The name means the Lord saves. God chose it himself.

In the Bible a name is a mission. The angel told Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). Every time we say the name of Jesus, we confess what he came to do.

Paul tells us that because Jesus humbled himself to the cross, God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend (Philippians 2:9–10). That is why we bow our heads at his name.

Peter, standing before the council, said: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not know what this year will bring. But we know the name in which we will face it.

So let us begin the year as the Church begins it: in the name of Jesus. Let it be the first word on our lips in the morning and the last at night. And may the Lord bless us and keep us in his name throughout this year. Amen.

opts.a: Mary, Mother of God, and the year ahead
intro: In 431 the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God. The first day of the year belongs to her and to her Son.

sub: Not mother of a man only.
The Son she bore is God.
Ephesus defended Christ by honouring Mary.
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: The shepherds' report.
Mary keeps it in her heart.
A heart that remembers God's deeds.
points.apply: Each night this year, recall one thing God did that day.

sub: Born of a woman.
So that we might be children.
Abba, Father.
points.apply: Put your family under Mary's protection for the year.

concl: Mary, Mother of God, is also our mother.
With her we begin the year pondering God's works in our hearts.
opts.resolve: I will entrust this year to Mary, Mother of God, and keep a habit of thanksgiving each night.
homily: Dear friends, today the Church greets Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In the year 431 the bishops gathered at Ephesus defended this title, because the Child she bore is not a man who later became God, but the eternal Son of God made man. Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
Paul says: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). God did not come among us from nowhere. He came through a mother, through a family, through a people.

When the shepherds told what they had seen, Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She did not understand everything, but she kept it and turned it over in prayer. That is a good way to live a year.
Paul adds: because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6). Through Mary's Son we become children of God.

So let us begin the year with her. Let us ask Mary, Mother of God, to keep our families, and let us learn from her to ponder each day what God has done. And may the Lord bless us and keep us, and give us peace. Amen.

intro: Theme: “Begin the year in the name of Jesus.”
On the eighth day the Child received the name the angel had given: Jesus, “God saves”. We begin the new year not with luck or fear but with a name: the name above every name.

points.h: The name that reveals who he is
sub: At the burning bush God revealed his name to Moses: a name to be remembered for all generations.
In Jesus that name becomes a person: “God saves”.
Mary and Joseph obey the angel: they give the name God chose.
q: This is my name forever, and this my title for all generations.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Say the name of Jesus with reverence; never use it carelessly.

points.h: There is no other saving name
sub: The prophets promised: whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Peter proclaimed: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
In every need of the coming year, call on this name with faith.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Make the short prayer “Jesus, I trust in you” your companion this year.

points.h: A new year, a new self
sub: The priests of Israel blessed the people by placing God's name upon them.
Mary and Joseph presented the Child to the Lord; we present this new year to him.
St Paul tells us to put off the old self and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness.
q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Write one resolution for the year that will make you more like Christ, and offer it at the altar today.

concl: Whatever this year brings, it is placed under the name of Jesus.
Let us begin it blessed, cleansed and renewed, calling on the name that saves.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26 at the start of each month this year.
